title: parity-layer: unify chatv1 params, stabilize tool handshake and framed response envelope
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: parameter normalization and stronger stream/tool handshake. No breaking changes expected; improved streaming resilience and clearer stop/logprob semantics for compatibility with downstream clients.
description:
Context: Customers and downstream SDKs expect parity with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions semantics for param names, role preservation, stop and logprob behavior, and the shape/handshake of streaming function/tool call envelopes. This PR aims to close several incompatibilities observed during the recent migration pilots: (1) inconsistent acceptance/aliasing of v1 params (temperature, top_p, n, stop variants), (2) loss or collapse of role/metadata on fragments when streaming tools/function outputs, (3) ambiguity in stop token handling when multiple stop sources are present, and (4) intermittent stream framing failures under backpressure that broke tool-handshake/hand-off in high-throughput scenarios.
Summary of changes: 1) Param normalization layer: added a single translation table and coercion pass in the openai_compat adapter to accept common v1 aliases (eg: "temperature" | "temp", "top_p" | "topP"), coerce numeric types and validate mutually-exclusive configs (n + stream combos guarded). 2) Role & metadata preservation: stream fragments now attach an immutable role_id header and compact role metadata blob that survives chunking; role metadata is re-stitched at the stream coalescer to produce consistent role fields in framed JSON envelope. 3) Stop/logprob semantics unification: introduced stop-source weighting in the scorer so when multiple stop signals arrive (model-level EOS, user-supplied stop array, tool-inserted sentinel) we deterministically prioritize and emit a single canonical stop event and a best-effort logprob envelope describing the reason. 4) Tool/function handshake stabilization: implemented a two-phase handshake on stream start (capability advertisement + tool schema confirmation) and graceful fallback to framed-tool-text mode when the client does not accept rich tool envelopes. 5) Stream framing & backpressure fixes: improved coordinator's chunking heuristics, added heartbeat keepalive and an adaptive retry/backoff for transient write errors to avoid tearing stream boundaries. 6) SDK adapters and docs: small SDK compatibility helpers (Python and TS) plus an expanded docs note describing the framing envelope and expected client behavior.
Testing & CI: unit tests added for parameter aliasing, stop arbitration cases, and tool handshake state machine. Integration: end-to-end streaming tests with the python SDK and a lightweight Go client reproduced earlier flakes and are now stable on CI after two retries. A flaky harness test (tests/integration/test_streaming_high_load.py) required a test timeout bump and a small harness sleep to avoid racy client shutdown; we captured this as a test-only change.
Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature-flag (openai_compat.v1_parity) — enabled for internal smoke and 10% of prod traffic for two days, then ramp to 100% if no regressions.
Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled; clients using raw v1-like params will now be accepted and normalized (no API key or auth change).
Todo/Follow-ups: publish a small migration note to customers using custom stream parsers (ENG-4900), add observability for stop-source frequencies (ENG-4912), and run a perf canary for peak-traffic streaming.
Checklist: - [x] Param normalization implementation - [x] Role metadata persistence across fragments - [x] Deterministic stop/logprob arbitration - [x] Tool handshake fallback mode - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs update Related Linear: ENG-4821 (openai v1 parity), ENG-4837 (stream stability), ENG-4900 (customer migration)

review_comments: Alexei Dobry: Please add a short explainer for the stop-source priority table and why tool-originated sentinels should be lower priority than model-eos. Also prefer a deterministic tie-breaker instead of random selection.
Priya Kapoor: Added a deterministic priority map (model_eos > user_stop > tool_sentinel) and documented tie-break behavior in code comments and openai_compat.md.

Samara Liu: The two-phase handshake looks fine but can we avoid an extra roundtrip for clients that already advertise accepted_envelopes? Consider piggybacking on the initial capability advertisement.
Priya Kapoor: Good suggestion — initial capability advert now includes accepted_envelopes and we short-circuit confirmation for known-legacy clients. Kept fallback for unknown clients.
Diego Marin: Noticed a potential race in fragment coalescer when a heartbeat triggers a flush concurrently with a tool handoff. Added a mutex and a unit test reproducer.
Priya Kapoor: Fixed with mutex and added test; also added a small explanatory comment in fragment_coalescer around concurrency model.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash; CI green after rerun. No post-merge failures observed in canary window.
notes_for_release: Feature gated. When enabled the adapter will accept v1-style param names and emit a consistent framed JSON envelope for tool outputs; clients that relied on ad-hoc stream framing should read docs/openai_compat.md before upgrading.
manual_steps: 1) Flip feature flag in helm values for staging. 2) Run smoke suite against python SDK. 3) Monitor stop_source metrics and stream error rate for 48h.
known_limitations: - Very large role metadata blobs are truncated to 8KB to avoid excessive memory churn; this may affect unusual custom metadata. - Some third-party parsers that split purely on newline boundaries will need minor updates to handle the framing envelope.
